positions.commentary: The speaker uses Microsoft as an example of understanding how a company changes over time, noting the importance of understanding the trajectory from 2011 to 2016.
The speaker previously held a value investor mindset that Netflix was not worth its valuation, but later corrected this mistake and believes the company will benefit from industry shakeouts.
Dollar Tree has become a meaningful part of the speaker's portfolio, and he has followed the company for a decade, eventually acting on his positive thoughts regarding management and strategy.
Five Below is used as an example of a small retailer where the quality and confidence of the merchant team is really important to how the business does over time.

thesis: This episode argues that investors must understand how companies evolve over time, using Microsoft's trajectory as a key example. It also emphasizes the importance of merchant team quality for small retailers like Five Below and highlights the value of following a company's management and strategy over a decade, as seen with Dollar Tree.

claims.claim: The speaker previously held a value investor mindset that Netflix was not worth its valuation, but later corrected this mistake and believes the company will benefit from industry shakeouts.
claims.quote: I had a very typical value investor mindset on for a long time of, you know, there's no way look at the numbers. There's no way this thing's worth whatever the numbers were at that time, 30, 40, 50 billion dollars. And let that stop me from truly learning about the company and thinking about what they were trying to do and where the industry was going. I corrected that mistake later on

claims.claim: Dollar Tree has become a meaningful part of the speaker's portfolio, and he has followed the company for a decade, eventually acting on his positive thoughts regarding management and strategy.
claims.quote: Dollar Tree, which is a retailer here in the US that's become a meaningful part of my portfolio. And I've I've basically followed it at this point. I've probably followed the company for a decade. And I and I never owned it until. And again, people can check this at TSOH, but I think it was some point in the middle last year or late last year.

claims.claim: The speaker uses Microsoft as an example of understanding how a company changes over time, noting the importance of understanding the trajectory from 2011 to 2016.
claims.quote: to truly understand why the Microsoft of 2016 was different than the Microsoft of 2011, at least directionally or in terms of trajectory, it was massively important to understand that.

claims.claim: Five Below is used as an example of a small retailer where the quality and confidence of the merchant team is really important to how the business does over time.
claims.quote: Like an example, it comes to mind for me, is five below, which is a retailer in the US. Their merchant team basically turned over, and for a small retailer, the quality and confidence of your merchant team is really, really important to how your business does over time.
